$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH -- EDIT THIS FILE.

The two MSPDI custom-field frames GRS borrows to carry Task.fadeInDays and Task.fadeOutDays (AT-40 / AT-41 of table T-058). The rules for using them are EX-6 and EX-8 of table T-033; this file holds only the values those rules need.

THE NUMBERS BELOW ARE A QUOTATION, NOT A GRS DECISION. They are members of Microsoft's PjCustomField enumeration and mean nothing GRS chose. Source: https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/VBA-Docs/blob/main/api/Project.PjCustomField.md

WARNING -- the committed canon does not carry these two numbers. docs/reference/mspdi/ names only pjCustomTaskText1 = 188743731 (learn-docs/project-xml-data-interchange/fieldid-element.md:54) and pjCustomResourceCost1 = 205521019 (same file, :58). The external table is the only source for Number1 and Number2. What can be checked locally is that the SAME external table gives pjCustomTaskText1 = 188743731, which matches fieldid-element.md:54 and the worked example at custom-field-data-in-xml.md:52 to the digit -- two independent sources agreeing is why the table is trusted for the other two.
Rebuild: npm run gen   |   npm run gen:check fails if anything has drifted.
Validated by _source/mspdi-custom-fields.schema.json before a byte is written.

cfType.why: Duration (CFType 2) is not used: it carries a DurationFormat and invites the partner to give the value a calendar meaning. A fade is a count of days that does not walk the calendar.

aliasNote: EVERY alias IS EMPTY ON PURPOSE. It is written into the partner's file and shows as a column heading in the partner's tool, and it is also the key EX-6 uses to tell a frame GRS wrote from a frame the import source wrote. It is NOT a word the screen prints, so it is not in display-words.json and MUST NOT be translated. Until the user fills it, GRS cannot recognise its own frame and must not claim one.
